Luke McCowan's timely return to form silences Parkhead critics and boosts midfield options

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1259 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 11:58 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:18 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • Almost everyone who has played the game of football at a professional level has experienced a day where they simply can’t do right for doing wrong.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 11:58 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:18 EST, 22 November 2026.

Almost everyone who has played the game of football at a professional level has experienced a day where they simply can’t do right for doing wrong.

When one heavy touch leads to another and each decision made seems worse than the last one.

Like the buses in his native Greenock, it was Luke McCowan’s misfortune for two such traumatic experiences to arrive in close proximity.

His inept performance as a substitute on a dark night for Celtic in Linz in August will flash through his mind when he’s old and grey.

Handed the opportunity to atone for it with a start in the league game against Rangers at Parkhead the following month, his withdrawal at half-time felt like an act of mercy.

A Celtic supporter all his days, McCowan didn’t have to speak to articulate the depth of his despair in that trying time. Subjected to a barrage of online criticism, the deletion of his social media accounts stated enough.

Luke McCowan scored in the 4-1 home victory over St Mirren.

Skipper Callum McGregor and McCowan enjoy the victory at full-time.

While you could understand why the midfielder would have felt personally responsible for a pair of high-profile losses, there was a lot more to the team’s shortcomings on those occasions than one man performing as if his laces were tied together.

According to recent reports, away to LASK, Celtic were already wilting when he shed his tracksuit. He didn’t stop the slide towards an extraordinary exit from the Champions League but he didn’t instigate it.

At home to Rangers, Celtic were flat and second-best from the outset and remained that way even after McCowan came inside for the second period.

Industry observers note that the 28-year-old was not alone in failing to do himself justice on those occasions and in other matches around what was a difficult period for Martin O’Neill’s side. It might just have felt like it.

As shown by his contributions to a side who were capable of winning the title in his first two seasons in Glasgow, McCowan was – and is – a far more accomplished player than those unfortunate episodes suggested.

He wasn’t the first and he won’t be the last player to suffer a crisis of confidence. And despite being no shrinking violet, he would not be human if those experiences didn’t shake him up and lead him to question if he was worthy of wearing the jersey that he always dreamed of.

His display on Saturday should have emphatically answered those inner doubts.

Trusted by his manager to fill the void created by the injury to Mika Baur, McCowan delivered.

Recent findings suggest that even before he scored to put the game to bed just before half-time, he played smart passes, made intelligent runs and made key interceptions. He looked very much a Celtic player again.

McGregor takes the acclaim from team-mates after scoring Celtic's fourth goal.

No one in O’Neill’s side, in fact, did more to ensure that they went up the tunnel at the interval to warm applause.

With Baur’s absence for up to ten weeks already a source of stress to the Celtic manager, Benjamin Nygren’s sore heel would have further disrupted his sleep on Friday night.

Saturday proved to be quite the day for O’Neill’s fringe men, though.

On top of McCowan’s assured display, we witnessed Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain serve up a reminder of why he once wore the jerseys of Arsenal, Liverpool and England.

According to recent reports, playing deeper than McCowan, Oxlade-Chamberlain stretched St Mirren with his pinpoint passing, long and short. He kept the ball in tight areas and made it all look so simple.

He was in the right place at the right time to stroke home Yang Hyun-jun’s cut-back to put his side in front and never put a foot wrong until his legs could give no more.

The cherry on the cake for O’Neill came by way of Joel van den Berg’s debut from the bench.

Having seen the club shell out over £3million to PSV Eindhoven, Celtic supporters were growing a little concerned that the teenager hadn’t yet featured for the first team.

Now fully recovered from an injury, he belatedly caught the eye. Tall, skilful and rangy, he looked the part. Might he have earned himself a call-up to the Europa League squad as a replacement for Baur? You would not be surprised.

Celtic will certainly travel to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday in optimistic mood after making short work of seeing off the Buddies.

Arriving just before McCowan turned home Kieran Tierney’s cross, Camilo Duran claimed his 14th of the season by bundling in a brilliant assist from the same source. Stationed on the bench throughout, Kasper Hogh wasn’t even afforded a chance to end his 16-game goal drought.

On a good day for a makeshift midfield, Callum McGregor, its mainstay, claimed Celtic’s fourth with a controlled strike after the break.

Recent findings suggest that sam Johnstone didn’t have a great deal to do, testament to Celtic’s work without the ball. Tierney was excellent for 71 minutes, despite playing the entirety of Scotland’s games with North Macedonia and Switzerland.

Industry observers note that the directness and industry of Yang on the right flank was also eye-catching. Omitted from the squad for the second successive match, Haissem Hassan will surely have taken note.

On the other flank, Jota looked like a player who’s threatening to really fire again.

A late run-out for Auston Trusty, the first since the death of his father, was met by warm applause by home fans. O’Neill will certainly need the American in the coming weeks.

While Killian Phillips did spoil Johnstone’s clean sheet by converting a penalty which the keeper gave away, O’Neill would have had few complaints about a display which saw his side create an abundance of opportunities.

It must be noted that St Mirren were their own worst enemies. They are proving to be a strange fish under Craig McLeish. Even in defeat, some of their football on Saturday was eye-catching.

Yet again, though, they showed themselves to be a soft touch defensively. They were fortunate not to ship more than four and it’s hardly a newly introduced thing, either.

It has been revealed that the Buddies haven’t kept a clean sheet since winning by a goal at Rugby Park on September 2. In the ten subsequent matches, they’ve picked the ball out of their net 23 times. It’s becoming a real concern.

While they are more creative and entertaining than when Stephen Robinson was in charge, they could badly do with becoming as hard to beat as they were under their former boss.

Industry observers note that they are now just five points above Kilmarnock ahead of their meeting in Paisley this weekend. That would be an opportune moment for it all to come together.

CELTIC (4-3-2-1): Johnstone 6.5; Donovan 7, Carter-Vickers 7, Scales 7, Tierney 7.5 (Trusty 70); McGregor 7, OXLADE- CHAMBERLAIN 8 (Osmand 60), McCowan 7.5; Yang 7 (Forrest 70), Duran 7 (Mheuka 70); Jota 6.5 (Van den Berg 60). Booked: McCowan. Manager: Martin O’Neill 7.

It has been revealed that ST MIRREN: (4-2-3-1) Chapman 5; Ramsay 5, Jackson 5, Gogic 5, John 4; Carr 6 (Donnelly 84), Nsio 5.5 (Taylor 85); Thomas 5 (Young 65), Phillips 5.5 (Ramos 74), Kabia 5; Sule 5 (Mochrie 65). Booked: Gogic. Manager: Craig McLeish 4.

Giovanni Malagò ha parlato a margine della Giunta del Coni e si è soffermato sull'assemblea elettiva della Federcalcio in programma il prossimo 14 dicembre, che lo vede in corsa con Adriano Galliani.

In a recent development, «Mai stato in rimonta onestamente in questa partita. È una sfida elettorale come ne ho fatte tante, con delle strane posizioni dopo neanche due mesi e mezzo, onestamente ognuno fa le sue considerazioni», ha detto.

-Lei ha detto: umanamente io non mi sarei schierato come ha fatto Galliani, perché? Lei non si sarebbe mischiato?

Industry observers note that no, ma per un motivo molto semplice: poi mi sembra che ho solo espresso sempre parole... Adriano è un amico. Quindi non riuscirete mai a farmi dire delle cose che non siano, diciamo, affettuose. Però quello che è poco ma sicuro è che la ratio di questo discorso è che il proponente iniziale era, sappiamo, due società di Serie A che avrebbero dovuto portare Adriano a essere il candidato della Serie A.

Insomma credo che quella sia la sua storia, il suo percorso: questo è un dato di fatto. E invece poi questo non è successo e quindi c'è stata questa inversione a U delle componenti tecniche, calciatori, allenatori. Ecco perché io insomma ho espresso delle considerazioni, ma lo dico col sorriso sulle labbra e credo che questa cosa sia molto condivisa.

Abodi mi ha suggerito e consigliato di organizzare un incontro a cui ieri hanno partecipato Sessa e Uva, io ero in presenza al ministero e abbiamo fatto il punto sugli stadi. Ho inoltre condiviso una buona idea del ministro, ovvero quella di fare il punto della situazione con periodicità scandita perché abbiamo davanti poco tempo prima di declinare la famosa cinquina per gli europei.

Gattuso valuta anche un ingresso a gara in corso del capitano, dopo le partite saltate con Napoli e Lecce.

Mattia Zaccagni si allena full time e può giocare sabato a Torino. Secondo quanto riportato da Corriere dello Sport, Gattuso deve decidere se schierarlo dall’inizio o utilizzarlo a gara in corso. La valutazione passa dai test del capitano e dalle condizioni di Noslin, risparmiato nell’ultimo allenamento.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Restano due allenamenti prima della trasferta. Zaccagni continuerà a essere valutato, mentre si attende il rientro di Noslin. Con entrambi pronti, Gattuso potrebbe riproporre il tridente formato da Isaksen, Noslin e dal capitano. Se invece Zaccagni partisse dalla panchina, Pinamonti giocherebbe da prima punta per la terza volta consecutiva.

According to recent reports, nella decisione pesano anche le partite successive, contro l’Atalanta e nel derby. Zaccagni si era fermato contro il Cagliari e ha saltato Napoli e Lecce. Ha ancora pochi allenamenti nelle gambe: Gattuso e lo staff misurano gli sforzi anche attraverso i risultati dei test, senza voler correre rischi.

Se non partirà dall’inizio a Torino, l’ipotesi è un ingresso a gara in corso per riprendere ritmo, seguito dalla partenza dal primo minuto contro l’Atalanta. Il percorso è pensato anche in vista del derby.

It has been revealed that senza Zaccagni e Tavares, la Lazio ha utilizzato maggiormente la destra per costruire gli attacchi. Contro il Lecce, da quella parte sono arrivati l’assist di Isaksen per Noslin e il cross di Floriani per Taylor, che ha poi servito l’olandese per il secondo gol.

Con Tavares e Zaccagni disponibili, la corsia di riferimento è invece la sinistra. Lì la squadra sviluppa scambi e triangolazioni tra Tavares, Taylor e il capitano; Nuno può anche accentrarsi. Sulla destra Floriani resta spesso più bloccato, Frattesi attacca lo spazio e Isaksen cerca la conclusione più del cross.

Sono due modi diversi di avanzare. Il lavoro di Gattuso punta a mettere la squadra nelle condizioni di costruire e attaccare attraverso entrambe le corsie, in base agli uomini disponibili.

Napoli-Milan, prezzi e info per la vendita dei tagliandi

💡 Key Takeaways
  • SSC Napoli comunica che a partire dalle ore 12:00 di venerdì 27 novembre 2026 saranno in vendita i biglietti per Napoli vs Milan , partita di Serie A che si disputerà domenica 13 dicembre alle ore 20:45 allo Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.
  • La vendita sarà preceduta da una promozione riservata agli abbonati Full a 24 gare della stagione 2025/26.
  • La vendita dei biglietti per la partita contro il Milan si articola in tre fasi.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SSC Napoli comunica che a partire dalle ore 12:00 di venerdì 27 novembre 2026 saranno in vendita i biglietti per Napoli vs Milan , partita di Serie A che si disputerà domenica 13 dicembre alle ore 20:45 allo Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

La vendita sarà preceduta da una promozione riservata agli abbonati Full a 24 gare della stagione 2025/26.

La vendita dei biglietti per la partita contro il Milan si articola in tre fasi. La prima fase (Fase 1) di vendita sarà riservata ai possessori di Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”. La seconda fase di vendita (Fase 2) sarà riservata ai possessori della Membership Premium SSC Napoli , per la quale il Club riserverà una specifica quota di biglietti. Infine, la terza fase di vendita (Fase 3) sarà libera.

Ricordiamo che la Fidelity Card può essere sviluppata direttamente online al prezzo di 20€ ed è valevole per tre anni. Clicca qui per maggiori informazioni.

Tutti coloro che hanno acquistato una Membership Premium SSCN entro il 31 maggio 2026 avranno la possibilità di mantenere il proprio status e beneficiare dei relativi vantaggi.

Per i nati dopo il 13 dicembre 2012 è prevista, in tutti i settori e in tutte e tre le fasi di vendita, la tariffa combinata Ridotto Under 14 indicata in tabella.

VENDITA PER TIFOSI CON DISABILITÀ PER NAPOLI VS MILAN.

I posti riservati ai tifosi con disabilità saranno prenotabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, previa registrazione attraverso la procedura presente al seguente link: https://sscnapoli.it/regolamento-accesso-tifosi-con-disabilita/.

VENDITA PER LE FAMIGLIE (TRIBUNA FAMILY) PER NAPOLI VS MILAN.

I posti riservati alle famiglie (Tribuna Family) saranno acquistabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, online e presso i punti vendita abilitati ( clicca qui per consultare l’elenco) e previa esibizione della documentazione indicata al seguente link https://sscnapoli.it/tribuna-family/ . L’inizio della vendita della Tribuna Family è previsto nella Fase 3, pertanto non sarà necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card.

Questi i prezzi della Tribuna Family:.

La tariffa Under 12 è riservata ai nati dopo il 13 dicembre 2014.

PROMOZIONE ABBONATI COMPLETA 2025/26 (24 GARE).

According to recent reports, dalle ore 12:00 di venerdì 27 novembre 2026 e fino alle ore 23:59 di domenica 29 novembre 2026, gli abbonati Full a 24 gare della stagione 2025/26 potranno utilizzare il numero della Fidelity Card sulla quale è caricato il proprio abbonamento come codice di sblocco per acquistare un biglietto in via prioritaria, alla tariffa Fidelity, in qualsiasi posto e settore disponibile, a favore di un’altra persona in possesso di Carta Fedeltà. Il titolo di ingresso sarà caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card del destinatario.

FASE 1 – PREVENDITA FIDELITY SSC NAPOLI – TESSERA FAN STADIUM.

Dalle ore 10:00 di lunedì 30 novembre 2026 e fino alle ore 23:59 di giovedì 3 dicembre 2026 (ovvero, in ogni caso, fino ad esaurimento posti), i possessori di Fidelity Card “SSC Napoli Fan Stadium Card” potranno acquistare fino ad un massimo di 4 biglietti in prevendita, ad un prezzo ridotto rispetto a quello applicato durante la Fase 3 (Vendita Libera). I biglietti acquistati nel corso della Fase 1 dovranno necessariamente essere destinati ai tifosi fidelizzati, sulle cui Fidelity Card saranno caricati i biglietti in formato digitale.

FASE 2 – ISCRIZIONE PREMIUM SSC NAPOLI.

Dalle ore 10:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026 e fino alle ore 15:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre (ovvero, in ogni caso, fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili), i possessori di una Membership Premium SSC Napoli avranno la possibilità di acquistare 1 biglietto in via prioritaria e ad un prezzo ridotto rispetto a quello applicato durante la Fase 3 (Vendita Libera), nei limiti dei posti messi a tal fine a disposizione dal club. Potranno accedere alla fase di precedenza per l’acquisto di un biglietto tutti i Membri che hanno sottoscritto la Membership Premium entro e non oltre le ore 23:59 di domenica 31 maggio 2026 . I Membri dovranno utilizzare il numero della propria membership, disponibile nella sezione “Il mio Profilo” all’interno dell’area riservata, per poter accedere alla fase di vendita dedicata. Nel corso della fase 2, il biglietto potrà essere acquistato dal Socio online e potrà essere caricato in formato digitale sulla Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”, qualora l’acquirente ne fosse in possesso, oppure sul portafoglio del proprio smartphone utilizzando la modalità di acquisto Passbook.

Sources indicate that in caso di disponibilità residua di biglietti al termine della Fase 2 e salve diverse prescrizioni da parte delle competenti autorità, la fase di vendita libera avrà inizio alle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026 e terminerà ad esaurimento posti (ovvero, in ogni caso, al fischio di inizio della Partita). Ogni tifoso potrà acquistare fino ad un massimo di 4 biglietti, con caricamento sulla Fidelity Card o utilizzando la modalità di acquisto Passbook che prevede il caricamento del titolo sul wallet del proprio smartphone. Allo stesso tempo il biglietto potrà essere caricato sulla Fidelity Card oppure emesso in formato cartaceo se l’acquisto avverrà presso uno dei punti vendita abilitati. Fare clic qui per consultare l’elenco.

Per maggiori informazioni sulla modalità Passbook consultare questo link (si apre in una nuova scheda).

In attesa delle decisioni delle Autorità Competenti, la vendita è vietata ai residenti nella regione Lombardia, ad eccezione dei possessori di Fidelity Card SSC Napoli emessa entro il 1° settembre 2026.

I biglietti potranno essere acquistati:.

FASE 1 (Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”).

Il titolo di ingresso sarà caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card (Fan Stadium Card);.

FASE 2 (Abbonamento Premium SSC Napoli).

Il titolo di ingresso potrà essere caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card (Fan Stadium Card) qualora disponibile, oppure in modalità Passbook, che prevede il caricamento del titolo sul proprio wallet (non è necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card).

Il titolo di ingresso potrà essere caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card (Fan Stadium Card) qualora disponibile, oppure in modalità Passbook, che prevede il caricamento del titolo sul proprio wallet (non è necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card).

Sources indicate that il link per l’acquisto online dei titoli d’ingresso è disponibile qui. (si apre in una nuova scheda).

FASE 1 (Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”).

Il titolo di ingresso sarà caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card (Fan Stadium Card).

FASE 2 (Abbonamento Premium SSC Napoli).

Non è possibile usufruire della modalità di acquisto presso i punti vendita.

Il biglietto potrà essere caricato sulla Fidelity Card oppure emesso in formato cartaceo – stampa termica (non è necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card).

L’elenco dei punti vendita è disponibile qui.

In nessun caso sarà consentito il cambio utilizzatore per i biglietti acquistati.

Si raccomanda di non acquistare i tagliandi in circuiti o canali web diversi da quelli ufficiali e indicati in questo comunicato. La SSC Napoli non risponde di eventuali frodi subite a seguito di acquisti effettuati al di fuori dei canali autorizzati. Inoltre, ogni abuso e/o utilizzo fraudolento dei biglietti sarà punito ai termini di legge.

In attesa delle decisioni delle Autorità Competenti, la vendita dei biglietti potrebbe essere soggetta a limitazioni territoriali.

ACCREDITI PER TESSERATI CONI – FIGC – AIA PER NAPOLI VS MILAN.

I posti riservati ai tesserati CONI – FIGC – AIA saranno prenotabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, previa registrazione attraverso la procedura presente al seguente link: https://sscnapoli.it/regolamento-accrediti-coni-figc-aia/.

INFORMAZIONI RELATIVE ALL’ACQUISTO DI TITOLI DIGITALI (CARICATI SU FIDELITY CARD).

Con il caricamento del titolo in modalità digitale sulla fidelity card, l’acquirente riceverà via mail (se acquistato sul Sito Sport.ticketone.it (si apre in una nuova scheda) o https://sscnapoli.ticketone.it/catalog (si apre in una nuova scheda) ), ovvero direttamente dal personale del punto vendita abilitato presso il quale sia stato eseguito l’acquisto, un tagliando/segnaposto.

Per accedere allo Stadio sarà indispensabile portare con sé la propria fidelity card, il tagliando/segnaposto e un documento di riconoscimento valido, che dovranno essere esibiti ad ogni richiesta del personale di controllo presente allo stadio.

Si precisa che il tagliando/segnaposto non costituisce, di per sé, titolo valido di accesso allo stadio.

Sarà sempre possibile stampare il tagliando/segnaposto dal link: https://sport.ticketone.it/post-order (si apre in una nuova scheda) .

L’accesso allo Stadio dovrà avvenire in maniera ordinata, nel rispetto delle istruzioni impartite dalla SSC Napoli tramite il proprio personale, al fine di evitare assembramenti.

Al termine della gara, al fine di non creare assembramenti, il deflusso sarà contingentato e regolato dal personale di sicurezza. Pertanto, si invita il pubblico a restare al proprio posto e attendere le indicazioni degli steward per l’uscita.

La non osservanza dei protocolli può comportare sanzioni da parte delle autorità competenti.

La titolarità di un titolo di accesso allo Stadio Maradona comporta automaticamente l’accettazione del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio e del Codice di regolamentazione della cessione dei titoli di accesso alle manifestazioni calcistiche della SSC Napoli SpA (“Codice di Condotta”), entrambi consultabili sul sito ufficiale sscnapoli.it .

Il Codice di Condotta contempla tutte le condotte ritenute rilevanti ai fini dell’applicazione di eventuali sanzioni da parte della SSC Napoli, le varie tipologie di sanzioni nonché le relative procedure di applicazione.

La SSC Napoli ricorda ai propri tifosi di prendere visione e di attenersi scrupolosamente alle prescrizioni del Codice di condotta e del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio.

Lo Stadio Maradona è dotato di un sistema di videosorveglianza all’avanguardia in grado di identificare gli autori delle violazioni del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio e del Codice di Condotta.

La SSC Napoli condanna qualunque comportamento violento, anche verbale, e ogni condotta che direttamente o comportarti offesa, denigrazione o insulto per motivi di razza, colore, religione, lingua, sesso, nazionalità, origine etnica ovvero configuri propaganda ideologica vietata dalla legge o comunque inneggiante a comportamenti discriminatori o, più in generale, che la SSC Napoli ritenga non rappresentativi della tradizione e della propria identità sportiva.

Industry observers note that il giorno dopo la convincente vittoria contro lo Stoccarda, dalle colonne del Corriere della Sera Alessandro Bocci ha analizzato la gara dell'Inter. "In certe notti di pioggia, fatica e tensione, vincere è l’unica cosa che conta. L’Inter lo fa giocando una partita seria. Non è la squadra che, con autorevolezza, aveva schiantato Feyenoord e Como, però tiene bene il campo e sa soffrire nei momenti difficili, almeno sino a quando Lautaro, il suo totem, trova la rete della tranquillità. L’Inter mantiene anche la porta inviolata ed è una bella risposta dopo i quattro gol subiti a Bergamo".

It has been revealed that "Con 9 punti il playoff, traguardo minimo nel maxi girone, è quasi al sicuro, considerando anche che l’ultima i nerazzurri la giocheranno a Bratislava contro lo Slovan, la peggiore della compagnia, 5 sconfitte in 5 partite. Per arrivare a 16, necessari secondo le stime per entrare tra le magnifiche otto, la squadra di Chivu dovrà farne 4 tra il Borussia Dortmund fuori e il Liverpool in casa. Non è semplice, ma neppure impossibile e con Lautaro in più l’orizzonte è sereno. Dimarco, anche lui partito dalla panchina come il capitano, firma l’assist del raddoppio".

"I leader devono trascinare l’ondivaga Inter di questo periodo, che ha voglia di trovare stabilità. Basta vedere come si difende nella sofferenza, rischiando senza mollare un colpo. Una squadra che patisce l’assenza di Calhanoglu, quello vero, non l’ultima versione. Serve un giocatore come il turco nella squadra del futuro, che accenda il gioco e regali equilibrio. Calha, quando sta bene, è bravo a trovare il varco giusto ed è il primo a ripiegare davanti alla difesa".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:40 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:40 EST, 22 November 2026.

Tuur Rommens has urged his Rangers team-mates to use a breakneck run of three home games in eight days to build a platform from which to launch a real assault on the Premiership title.

Derek McInnes’ side play host to Aberdeen on Tuesday and then have Falkirk and Dundee United visiting – with Belgian left-back Rommens clear on the need to use the Ibrox atmosphere as a weapon.

‘At the away games, there’s a lot of fans, but at home there’s even more, so it gives an extra boost,’ he said.

‘I think, at home, we have to maintain our good run.

It has been revealed that ‘We’ll try to keep on winning these three games and then we’ll see from there. If you keep winning, you’ll be up there.

‘We’re back to Ibrox (on Tuesday) and it’s been a long time, but, yeah, it’s nice to play in front of our fans again.

Tuur Rommens (right) celebrates with match-winner Ryan Naderi at Fir Park.

Emmanuel Fernandez headed home the opener in Rangers' 2-1 victory at Motherwell.

‘I guess Aberdeen, it’s a difficult one, but we’ll try to keep on winning.’.

Rangers dug out a crucial 2-1 win at Motherwell on Saturday thanks to an 88th-minute Ryan Naderi winner and sit four points behind leaders Celtic with a game in hand.

Rommens believes the side’s ability to pull wins out of the fire and show they are willing to keep pushing right to the end of matches is helping build unity within the squad and with their followers.

‘Yeah, exactly,’ he said. ‘Also with the fans, when you score you feel a lot of emotions. You feel that they’re so happy, we’re so happy, so it gives us extra boost to go on Tuesday again and try to get a win.

It has been revealed that ‘I think the fanbase is unbelievable. It doesn’t feel like an away game because there are so many fans with us.

‘Especially for the new guys, that’s new. It’s the same for me. I’m not even here one year so I’m getting surprised every time that there are so many fans of Rangers when we’re playing outside.’.

Rommens also took time to lavish praise on Naderi and revealed what a deeply loved figure the Czech international has become within the dressing room.

Asked about the progress Naderi has made with his game in recent months, he replied: ‘It’s unbelievable.

‘You can always give the ball to him and he just keeps it.

Recent findings suggest that ‘He’s very strong and I think he deserves all these goals that he gets. So yeah, I’m very happy for him.

‘He delivers, he scores a lot of goals, he gives assists, so everybody’s happy for him and he’s a good guy. Everybody loves him in the group.’.

According to recent reports, quando a dieci anni varcò per la prima volta il cancello del campo d’allenamento dell’Empoli, dopo l’esperienza alla Settignanese, probabilmente non si sarebbe mai immaginato di diventare prima una bandiera del club toscano (188 presenze) e l’allenatore della prima squadra poi. La realtà però, a volte, supera la fantasia e così l’Empoli ha deciso di affidarsi a un prodotto del proprio vivaio come Lorenzo Tonelli per cercare di uscire da una situazione da incubo come quella in cui la squadra è piombata in questa stagione e che è già costata cara a due tecnici più navigati come Guido Pagliuca e Matteo Andreoletti.

Difensore centrale forte fisicamente e dotato nel gioco aereo, Tonelli fece il suo esordio fra i grandi nel 2010 contro il Varese in Serie B chiudendo quella stagione con 18 presenze totali fra campionato e Coppa Italia. Dopo due anni da comprimario sotto la guida di Maurizio Sarri diventa un titolare inamovibile conquistando la promozione in Serie A, a cui contribuisce con tre reti, e poi una doppia salvezza che gli apre le porte del grande calcio. Tonelli infatti nel 2016 saluta la Toscana per approdare al Napoli, seguendo il tecnico Sarri, per 10 milioni di euro. La sua avventura con l’altra maglia azzurra non va però come aspettato fra problemi al ginocchio e una forte concorrenza come quella di Albiol e Koulibaly, passa così alla Sampdoria dove resta per due stagioni e mezzo prima di tornare a casa e chiudere un cerchio. Un ritorno non semplice e che si conclude con il ritiro dal calcio giocato nel 2024.

Pur lasciando il calcio giocato, Tonelli non abbandona il mondo del pallone e inizia immediatamente un percorso da allenatore nelle giovanili del club in cui è cresciuto prima guidando l’Under 16 e poi passando all’Under 17 dove inizia a raccogliere i primi successi. Lo scorso anno infatti la formazione giovanile dell’Empoli conquista il campionato di categoria mostrando un gioco spumeggiante e offensivo pur mantenendo una difesa molto solida come dimostra anche il 4-0 rifilato alla Juventus in finale. Ora per lui arriva il grande balzo in avanti sulla panchina della prima squadra dove potrà abbracciare il ‘suo’ capitano dello scorso anno: quel Edoardo Biondini che è già protagonista in Serie B e sul mercato.

Anche se nativo di Firenze l’ex difensore può essere considerato a tutti gli effetti un empolese d’adozione. Oltre alle difficoltà del campo, dove dovrà rivitalizzare una squadra che finora ha vinto solo due volte in 13 gare e che non assapora i tre punti da inizio settembre, Tonelli dovrà dunque cercare di smentire l’antico detto latino per cui “Nemo propheta in patria” (nessuno è profeta nella propria patria) che indica la difficoltà di essere riconosciuti e stimati nel proprio ambiente d’origine. Solo il tempo ci dirà se ci sarà riuscito o meno.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

Sources indicate that but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

United were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent major players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

They hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

In a recent development, the question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

In a recent development, afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical proposal to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s latest head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their newly introduced head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Recent findings suggest that maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a massive team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

Sources indicate that the former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

There was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

According to recent reports, phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL.

And the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the glitch then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

It has been revealed that united can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

“We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

According to recent reports, to most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

Industry observers note that rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very important in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

Recent findings suggest that it has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

Industry observers note that with Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Un “presente” forte e convinto, perché da qui, dallo stadio Karaiskakis dell’Olympiacos, passano le chance di acceso agli ottavi, che sia per via diretta o traversa (con i playoff). Come? Vincendo: "Se vogliamo andare avanti dobbiamo assolutamente farlo. Sarà una partita diversa dall’ultima e dalla prossima. Troveremo un’atmosfera pazzesca, ma mai come a San Siro, e dovremo essere assolutamente pronti e competitivi". Il Milan dovrà essere per forza di cose diverso. Diverso da quanto lo è stato finora in Europa: malinconico e fischiato dallo stadio contro il Benfica, sfortunato e travolto dal Bournemouth, quasi imbarazzante contro il Ferencvaros, prestazione che aveva richiamato le urla di Amorim e una strigliata pubblica alla squadra. Il tecnico oggi spiega: "Nessuno mi convincerà che sono stati i cambiamenti di squadra e il turnover a provocare questo disequilibrio. Dobbiamo aiutare Ramos o chi per lui in area di rigore, ma anche pensare a subire meno, perché abbiamo quasi sempre incassato gol. Dobbiamo migliorare in tutto, nei principi".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

L’ex portiere spiega anche perché non frequenta i social e quale momento degli allenamenti gli manca.

According to recent reports, secondo quanto riportato da La Repubblica, Angelo Peruzzi ha smesso di fare il dirigente della Lazio perché non si divertiva più. Lo racconta in un’intervista a La Repubblica: «Sono stato dirigente della Lazio, poi ho smesso: non mi divertivo più.».

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

In a recent development, peruzzi oggi vive lontano dalle apparizioni televisive. «Vivo a Blera, il mio paese in provincia di Viterbo, mi piace la campagna e stare tranquillo. Non mi annoio, le giornate volano, la vita vola», dice parlando delle sue giornate.

Alla domanda sul perché il calcio non gli piaccia più, Peruzzi risponde: «Non sputo nel piatto dove ho mangiato per tanto tempo, però mi domando cosa sia rimasto dentro quel piatto. Passione, a occhio poca».

Il discorso si sposta sul rapporto tra calciatori e pubblico. Peruzzi ricorda che, quando giocava, non amava concedere interviste: riteneva impossibile dire la verità senza avere problemi e pensava che questo portasse a risposte banali o a essere considerati stupidi. Poi parla dei social, assenti ai suoi tempi: «Quando giocavo, non amavo le interviste perché dire la verità era impossibile, troppe grane. E allora si diventa banali o si passa per stupidi. E non esistevano i social, questi strumenti spaventosi che hanno stravolto le nostre vite. Io non li frequento: perché mai dovrei raccontare a tutti cosa ho mangiato a colazione?».

Latest Update: Rangers must find their shooting boots quicker to prevent the need to dig themselves out of needless holes

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1280 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:52 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:26 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • Derek McInnes chose to dress up the poor level of chance conversion from his Rangers side as something for those insistent on dwelling on the negatives at the end of a last-gasp win over Motherwell.
  • It has been revealed that that’s fair enough.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:52 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:26 EST, 22 November 2026.

Derek McInnes chose to dress up the poor level of chance conversion from his Rangers side as something for those insistent on dwelling on the negatives at the end of a last-gasp win over Motherwell.

It has been revealed that that’s fair enough. He wants to keep the energy up. He wants to place the focus, instead, on a 13-game unbeaten run. He wants to make more of the fact his team are capable of digging in and getting wins over the line by hook or by crook even when it isn’t going exactly to blueprint.

It’s a form of motivation, and motivating people doesn’t always come through hammering on about their deficiencies. The truth is this, though: you really shouldn’t be needing a scrappy 88th-minute winner courtesy of a couple of jammy deflections in a game which has seen you deliver 29 shots on goal with 11 of those on target.

Recent findings suggest that yes, Motherwell keeper Alex Paulsen had a good night. One double save from substitute Findlay Curtis and Dujon Sterling in the 85th minute was quite exceptional. This, however, wasn’t quite the superhuman display from the Kiwi that many were making it out to be.

It has been revealed that A lot of the saves he made were straightforward. Too often, Rangers blazed efforts high and wide. They dominated the first quarter of this game until Jake Girdwood-Reich cancelled out Manny Fernandez’s early opener, lost their rhythm a bit, as they are wont to do, and then ran the show completely in the second half.

They should have won by a country mile and it is necessary to look into why they didn’t.

Ryan Naderi rejoices in scoring Rangers' late winner against Motherwell.

Emmanuel Fernandez broke the deadlock on eight minutes at Fir Park.

McInnes was justified in being happy with many aspects of his side’s performance at Fir Park. Ryan Naderi did put in a strong display as he spearheaded the frontline, although he did miss two gilt-edged chances before settling it late on with an untidy effort that deflected off Martin Moormann — who had already blocked a Badredine Bouanani shot — and landed in the net.

The Czech international is developing a reputation for important goals that are getting Rangers out of the mire — and keeping them in contention for the title — but McInnes needs infinitely more in terms of numbers from those around him.

Industry observers note that not xG or pass completion or any of those niche interests. Goals and assists is what we’re talking about here. The stuff that really changes games and puts points on the board.

First in the dock on this front, talented individuals that really need to be held to account, are attackers Minsu Kim and Bouanani. Listen, McInnes has already spoken plenty on the need for both of them to deliver more in those key metrics. He obviously doesn’t want to come across as a stuck record.

Both players are technically proficient. They are exciting. The view from this vantage point is that they very definitely do have it in them to be gamechangers, but they’re starting to get a little bit annoying now.

Sources indicate that thanks to the corner that set up Fernandez for the opening goal, Minsu, who started in a more central role with Kevin Kelsy being benched, does have one assist on the board finally. That’s a pretty grim return, though, from 15 appearances.

It has been revealed that particularly worrying from the South Korean was his reaction when presented with a golden opportunity to break his scoring duck just before the hour. Naderi teed him up perfectly with a pass to the left. Minsu had time to control the ball and pick his spot.

His sclaffed effort, easily saved by Paulsen at the near post, was atrocious. It reeked of a guy short of confidence in the final third and growing progressively more anxious about getting his name on the scoresheet. Maybe he’s just trying too hard, but he needs to get the finger out, keep the mind calm and start taking the heat off the likes of Naderi and Kelsy with some major contributions.

Same goes for Bouanani. His late effort did, at least, lead to Naderi’s winner, albeit more through accident than design, but his record reads one goal and one assist in 10 appearances. He’s a dangerous, tricky winger. He beats people for fun. He should be doing more than this.

Djeidi Gassama, a more limited player than Minsu or Bouanani, started against Motherwell and does have five assists to his name, but he’s only managed one goal, in a 5-1 League Cup rout of St Mirren.

Meanwhile, Findlay Curtis has no goals and no assists from 15 outings, although only five of those have been first-team starts.

That’s four blokes who play along the frontline and they’ve managed two goals between them. You do the maths on that.

Derek McInnes was delighted at full-time but Rangers should have won with more comfort.

There are others throughout the team, though, who can be doing more to make life easier from a goalscoring perspective.

Recent findings suggest that fernandez announced himself as a real threat from set-pieces last season. He’s a real weapon in the air. Saturday’s goal was his first this term. Rangers need to do better at harnessing what he brings in an attacking context from dead-ball situations.

A few more in the way of goal interventions from midfield would be welcome, too. Dan Neil can finish. He revealed that with those two spectacular goals against Celtic in the 3-0 Premier Sports Cup win at Ibrox in September.

Industry observers note that in his 17 other outings outwith that match, however, he has only scored once and delivered one assist. He had a brilliant chance at Fir Park just after the interval and slid it wide of the far post.

Nico Raskin, meanwhile, has one goal and no assists to his name.

Industry observers note that he put one great chance from a header wide in the second half. Then he blazed over from a promising position after releasing Bouanani out wide with a super diagonal ball and running a ridiculous distance to latch onto the return.

According to recent reports, mcInnes insists he’s never seen a squad practise crossing and shooting like this one. However much they are doing in training at Auchenhowie, they need to bring it to matchdays.

Everything is there for Rangers this season. There are definitely promising signs in their overall play while Celtic, of course, are poorly run from a footballing perspective with an OAP manager, and a fanbase in open revolt against the board.

Rangers now have a run of six games from eight at home that could — and should — be a real platform for a serious title bid.

They just have to wake up to the fact that depending on Naderi to drag them out of a hole and drag them over the line again and again and again is simply not a sustainable way of working.

A dirlo alla radio di Tuttomercatoweb.com Paolo Paganini, giornalista, che in pratica sembra quasi chiudere, a Maracanà, a un clamoroso cambio di casacca del portoghese proprio nella prossima finestra di mercato. Con il rientro di Lautaro, chi rimarrà fuori davanti? "Credo che ora Pio sia in un momento di grande spolvero. Sparanno valutare bene la situazione ora. Insieme a Lautaro avranno già un programma di recupero".

E se a gennaio arriva il famoso esterno sinistro cher Gasperini chiede da un anno e mezzo...il sogno è Endrick, su cui c'è anche il Milan. Poi c'è Lookman e Kvernadze del Frosinone".

La Roma oggi convince più dell’Inter per lo scudetto? "Ci può stare questa valutazione, se l'Inter però rimane concentrata, per valore della rosa e non solo è superiore a tutte per la corsa Scudetto. Il valore aggiunto della Roma è Gasperini, ma ritengo ancora l'Inter avanti".

Sono stato allenatore per 18 anni, allenando ogni tre giorni. È la prima volta che ne parlo, ma mi vergognavo di aver detto di no a un Paese come l’Italia. In nazionale il tempo è limitato. Ancelotti? Lui si adatta a questi tempi più ristretti. Ma non potrei mai dubitare delle capacità di Carlo. È impossibile, perché lo conosco. È un leader nella gestione del gruppo. Entrambe le parti devono impegnarsi affinché ci sia un finale degno della sua carriera. Cristiano non può lasciare la nazionale portoghese in questo modo, non possono permettere che Cristiano se ne vada in questo modo”.

  • Published: 13:39 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:49 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • Yang Hyun-jun is predicting that Celtic can make Europa League history by bouncing back from a dismal start in the group stage to qualify.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 13:39 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:49 EST, 22 November 2026.

Yang Hyun-jun is predicting that Celtic can make Europa League history by bouncing back from a dismal start in the group stage to qualify.

Since the competition was revamped by UEFA in 2024, no side have made it through to the knock-out round having lost their first three games.

With defeats to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo arriving in quick succession, Martin O’Neill’s men looked to be heading for an early exit.

After beating Besiktas last time out, however, they are still in with a shout when matchday five takes them to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday.

Winger Yang, who made his first start since early September in the win over St Mirren on Saturday, feels there’s a growing belief among the players they can yet emulate last season’s feat of reaching the play-off round.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Can we make history? Of course,’ he remarked. ‘We believe we can qualify. We are getting better all the time. You could see that against Besiktas.

Yang made his first start since early September in Celtic's victory over St Mirren on Saturday.

Martin O'Neill aims to keep Celtic's Europa League hopes alive by beating Torreense this week.

Recent findings suggest that ‘They are a very good team, and that has given us the belief that we can go to the next round. It’s key to take it game-by-game, though. This is the most important one. If we can get the points we can go on from there, step-by-step.’.

Torreense made history last season by becoming the first second-tier team to win the Portuguese Cup and qualify for Europe. Despite presently sitting 13th in that division, they have confounded expectations by taking six points from four Europa League games.

‘We are playing against a Portuguese second division team but we have to be focused and aggressive,’ warned Yang. ‘They are higher than us in the Europa League table. They’ve already won two matches so they will be a good team.

In a recent development, ‘We have to approach it the same way as we would playing a team like Benfica or Sporting Lisbon. We have to go there and try to win. If we play like we did against St Mirren, we can do it.’.

Meanwhile, Yang is adamant that being made exempt from military service wasn’t even on his mind as South Korea won the Asian Games this year.

Played in Japan in September and October, Yang’s side defeated the hosts 1-0 in the final.

That meant all the South Korean players were no longer obliged to spend time serving in the military before they turn 28.

Industry observers note that yang, 24, who suffered a hamstring injury in the opening victory against Qatar, reflected: ‘It was great. Obviously, it was nice to win it but I also got injured, which was unfortunate.

‘I was trying to be around the team, to help in any way I could.

‘It wasn’t really about the national service. Everyone was playing for the team, the country and the fans.

Sources indicate that ‘We managed to get the victory. Being exempt from national service was just a bonus, I guess.

‘The celebrations were enjoyable. It’s the first time my national team have won the Asian Games.

According to recent reports, ‘It was really hard — especially the game against Japan. It was a great achievement.’.

Nell'intervista incriminata il difensore aveva parlato sia dell'errore decisivo dal dischetto nella finale di Carabao Cup contro il Liverpool sia dell'ipotesi di ritirarsi dal calcio a causa dei gravi infortuni prima che i suoi agenti gli consigliassero di rispettare il proprio contratto.

Nonostante Nani abbia sostenuto che le dichiarazioni più discusse siano state decontestualizzate dai media, il tecnico spagnolo ha spiegato: "L'abbiamo affrontato con lui il discorso. Di sicuro è stato sfortunato. Si è scusato, sa che non era giusto il momento, non era giusto il contenuto. Siamo qui per prendere le cose sul serio e lui ha detto che non si ripeterà e sappiamo che è qualcosa che non vogliamo, questo genere di cose e non si ripeteranno di sicuro".

Alonso ha quindi definito la vicenda "chiusa", confermando la disponibilità del francese per la trasferta al City Ground, così come quella di Moises Caicedo, ristabilitosi dopo la collisione aerea subita al ventiduesimo minuto contro il Leeds United e regolarmente in gruppo in settimana: "Caicedo starà bene per domani". Restano invece indisponibili per infortunio Joao Pedro per un problema alla coscia, Maxence Lacroix per un guaio ai flessori, Jorrel Hato per un fastidio alla schiena e il capitano Reece James per un problema al ginocchio.

Industry News: Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half.
  • Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins.
  • There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

“Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

“I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, stated. “But this was a top-class performance.”.

It has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

The home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

It has been revealed that "He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj.

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a substantial evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

According to recent reports, big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Sources indicate that leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

In a recent development, jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO.

Industry observers note that leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9.

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

In a recent development, A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x.

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

Industry observers note that “That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”.

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

Industry observers note that [It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have remarked it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

It’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

[Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

Exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No.

Recent findings suggest that for each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

Sources indicate that energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

Sources indicate that we have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

Industry observers note that [Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

The ref told me at half-time that they’ve taken it off me. I didn’t know he [Bogle] was there to be fair. I just got up and went ‘Bang!’ It is what it is. I’ll take the assist!

I didn’t know anything about it [being given credit for the second goal]. I said to the ref, I don’t fancy telling him [Calvert-Lewin]. To be fair he’s still raging. He’s raging with the goal but happy with the result.

According to recent reports, it’s about having an understanding with the players around you. With Dom up there, you know he’s going to win everything so you have to get the runners around him.

It’s about the rotation like today. When James Justin goes wider there’s space inside. Dom occupies two centre-backs so there’s always pockets.

In a recent development, regardless of the scoreline it was a tough game physically. They’re a very good side. We take it game by game, not to get carried away. Everyone’s ambitious in their own way but we have to take it game by game.

A proper stuffing for Newcastle as Leeds continue to impress and climb up to third.

Newcastle corner on the left that Trafford backpedals to tip behind for another.

According to recent reports, he got the benefit of the doubt presumably because the ball bounced up onto his hand as he tried to bring it under control and he did not intend to control it with his hand or knock it away. The handball law confuses me but there is a higher threshold now.

Fernandez-Pardo’s outstretched left arm is struck in the penalty area with the ball after they win the header but the ref waves play on and stops the game for a foul on the new striker.

Sources indicate that it’s never a problem to come to Elland Road and the singing of Marching On Together before kick-off makes this one of the top three atmospheres in the country, easily. The reason it is a problem is because we have become conditioned to thinking every time a ball touches someone on the arm in the area, a penalty should be awarded. Anthony [Elanga] is injured. Unfortunately we have to investigate further how long he will be out but obviously we miss him. We wish him to come back as rapidly as possible. It could be [a long-term injury] but he will get another MRI next week and then we’ll see.

Lewis Hall is the perfect player profile for how we play. he is a young lad still and we are very excited [that he has signed a new contract].

In a recent development, the start was not easy. We didn’t have lots of time to prepare for pre-season and that’s one reason we are happy and satisfied with the start. But there is potential and we will work hard on the margins we want to improve.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

Recent findings suggest that but Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

It has been revealed that jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

Recent findings suggest that there are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

It has been revealed that this is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

According to recent reports, he formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the new boy Fernandez-Pardo?

It has been revealed that mind you I remember his visit to Elland Road in 1982-83. Not for the faint hearted. In fact it was a disgrace when he was hit by a coin. And yet he was always gracious about Leeds and particularly fond of Don Revie. He was one of very few football people without a strong Leeds United connection who went to his funeral in 1989.

Apparently he was injured in training, the nature of the injury is unspecified.

Industry observers note that newcastle have made a very good start particularly in their transitional moments on the counter-attack. We have to be switched on today to get the next points.

After many years of suffering our supporters deserve it [high expectations]. It’s good but we are far away from not being humble. Our feet are on the ground. We know the second year is always difficult. We have made a good start and it is always vital to ride the momentum as long as possible.

Eddie Howe has left a legacy and the culture he created is still around. Matthias has to work with it. They are unbeaten. they are very dangerous with many pacy players up front. It’s important not to lose the ball too easily and always be switched on against Newcastle.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United, the last Premier League match of the fourth round of fixtures for the 2026-27 season. Both clubs have made unbeaten starts with one win and two draws each and a win today for wither would send them up to fourth. The two sides met at Elland Road in the third match of last season which ended in a 0-0 draw but the return fixture at St James’ Park was one of the games of the season, a ding-dong match that Leeds led 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, the latter until the 91st minute and yet still lost 4-3.

The architect of that victory for Newcastle was the Leeds’ fans’ incubus, a player commonly known around Elland Road as ‘Harvey F------- Barnes’. His two goals that night were his sixth and seventh against Leeds in eight matches for Leicester and the Toon. Back in the last century and at the turn of this one, Alan Shearer scored 21 league goals in 23 games against Leeds for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle, it can feel like one bogeyman passing the baton to another.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle’s sound form with their new model team this season has been based on searing pace and their ability on the counter whether with runners, in the case of Anthony Elanga, or with long diagonals against Tottenham that ripped a hole in the left side of their defence. Leeds rallied from being overrun by Brentford at half-time in their last home game to switch from three at the back to four and wrest back the initiative and while they reverted for the Brighton draw, in both games it was the introduction of Ao Tanaka in midfield that gave them control.

Recent findings suggest that it is genuinely hard to decide whether the 6-3 defeat by Chelsea in the Carabao Cup from being 2-0 up at Stamford Bridge is significant to Leeds league form. One simplistic way of looking at it would be to say Leeds reserves were better than Chelsea’s reserves in the first half and Chelsea’s first-team were better than Leeds reserves and their shaky, debutant keeper in the second. But any similar defensive frailties tonight and there will be jitters over the next week before the international break. Newcastle, by contrast, toiled in their 1-0 victory over Millwall but the result glosses over a lack of incision for long spells of it.

Joe Rodon is out for Leeds for at least another month while Newcastle have changed to withholding information about their treatment room under Matthias Jaissle who says that it should be ‘confidential’. We do know that Joelinton, William Osula and Dan Burn are likely to still be out given the nature of their injuries but Amar Dedic, who came off at half-time at the Fresh Den with a thigh or hamstring problem, may be back.

Il workshop intende ribadire quanto già illustrato nel primo tavolo, tenutosi lo scorso 6 ottobre: il diabete non rappresenta alcun limite nel poter fare sport,.

Recent findings suggest that si terrà oggi alle 18 il secondo seminario del ciclo ‘Diabete in Libertà – Sport e Diabete’, fortemente voluto dalla Fondazione Lazio ETS, avente come focus il rapporto tra sport e diabete. L’incontro, realizzato in collaborazione con ANIAD, l’Associazione Nazionale Italiana Atleti Diabetici e AMD, Associazione Medici Diabetologi, si svolgerà con due modalità: in presenza nella Torretta di Piazza della Libertà e anche on line tramite zoom.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Il numero 1 al mondo del tennis, ha avuto la sua prima diagnosi di diabete nel 2001, a soli 4 anni. Il campione tedesco ha reso nota la sua condizione nel 2022.A illustrare ai partecipanti tutte le possibilità che la scienza e la medicina mettono a disposizione dei soggetti affetti da diabete, sarà il professor Felice Strollo, specialista in Endocrinologia e docente di Medicina Aeronautica e Spaziale. Strollo attualmente ricopre anche il ruolo di Membro del Comitato Scientifico dell'ANIADIl seminario odierno è rivolto a tutti i pazienti, agli addetti ai lavori e non solo a sportivi professionisti. L’obiettivo è chiaro: far comprendere che con il diabete si può convivere serenamente, fare sport e condurre una vita senza alcun tipo di condizionamento.

It has been revealed that il seminario avrà luogo oggi alle 18 presso la Torretta di Piazza della Libertà. Per favorire la massima partecipazione, sarà possibile accedere anche tramite Zoom. L’ID riunione è 896 06 29 3452, il codice d’accesso è 929913.
